_comment: PEtracer-style prime-editing recorder (Koblan, Yost et al., Science 2025, doi:10.1126/science.adx3800). Each cell carries ~12 barcoded lineage tracing cassettes of 3 edit sites, and each site stochastically receives one of 8 predefined 5nt marks. Editing is independent per site and irreversible, matching the published design; it is NOT sequential like DNA Typewriter. Reported kinetics are 0.05-0.1 edits per site per day over 2-3 weeks, and the paper reports 60-80% edit saturation as the band that maximises reconstruction accuracy.

prime_editing_backend._comment: marks_per_target draws the installed mark from an 8-entry alphabet per site. With 1 mark, independent edits at a site are indistinguishable and create homoplasy; with 8 they differ 7/8 of the time.

cell_type_dict._comment: Death holds the population to a workable size while lineages still accumulate divisions. Note that editing accrues per unit of SIMULATED TIME, not per division: the per-cell-cycle probability is converted to a hazard using cell_cycle_length, so expected saturation over sim_length T is 1 - (1 - p)^(T / cell_cycle_length). Here that is 1 - 0.9^11 = 0.69, inside the paper's 60-80% band. Realised generation depth runs higher than T and is reported by the run.
